steps.body: Twelve works the same way: ten and two more. The ten never gets recounted — only the two extras are new.
steps.narration: Twelve works the same way: ten and two more. The ten never gets recounted — only the two extras are new.

widget.prompt: A full group of 10 is already shown. Add the extra dots needed to make 12.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 2 dots still missing — the ten alone only makes 10, not 12.
1 leaves 1 dot still missing; ten and 1 is 11, one short of 12.
3 adds 1 too many; ten and 3 is 13, one past 12.

widget.missFeedback: The ten is done; count on from 10 while adding dots, and stop when you reach 12.
widget.successFeedback: 12 built — one complete ten and 2 more, exactly what the teen numeral says.

predict.prompt: Ten and two more — do you recount the ten?
predict.reveal: The ten is a finished, trusted chunk; only the newcomers need numbers.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb ten plus two.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb ten plus two rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 2. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 11 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 12.
13 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 2 hops from 10 to land on 12.

widget.missFeedback: Count 2 on from 10: you land on 12.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 2 more is 12 — the teen numeral written as a walk: ten first, then the ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 2 counts past ten are needed to reach 12.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 2 numbers, on 12.

widget.prompt: Build the four loose ones that join one finished ten to make 14.

commonCounts.feedback: That shows one too few loose ones. The target needs 4.
That shows one too many loose ones. Stop at 4.

widget.missFeedback: Keep the full ten fixed and build exactly 4 loose ones.
widget.successFeedback: 14 is one complete ten and 4 more.

widget.prompt: Why build the full ten before the extra ones?

options.label: It makes every teen have two full tens
options.feedback: A teen has one full ten, not two; two tens would make twenty.

options.label: It changes the value of each loose one
options.feedback: Each loose dot is still one, whether or not the ten is built first.

options.label: It lets us skip counting the extra ones
options.feedback: The extra ones still matter; the ten only gives a reliable starting point.

options.label: It anchors the teen as ten and some more
options.feedback: Correct — the full ten is a known group, so only the loose ones need to be counted.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 11? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 11 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 12.
13 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 11 lands on 12.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 11: you land on 12.
widget.successFeedback: 12 — one hop forward; the teens follow the song exactly.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 12.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 11 means one hop, stopping on 12.

widget.prompt: A group shows 14 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: That numeral names one more dot than the group shows.
Correct — a full ten and 4 more is what the numeral 14 says: 1 ten, 4 ones.
That numeral stops one dot short; the ten plus the extras reaches 14.
4 counts only the extras and forgets the whole completed ten underneath.
